screening_decisions.reason: Case-control study of women 15-44 years assessing VTE risk associated with low-estrogen COC use. Includes healthy women without predisposing conditions.
Prospective cohort study assessing VTE risk factors including oral contraceptive use in general population. Reports OR for OC use.
This is a mechanistic study measuring coagulation parameters, not clinical VTE outcomes. No actual venous thrombosis events studied.
Hospital-based case-control study of women with first episode of idiopathic DVT or PE, assessing OC use as risk factor.
Case-control study of nonpredisposed women under 40 with suspected DVT/PE, assessing current OC use association with VTE.
Methodological paper about network meta-analysis techniques, not a primary study of COC and VTE.
Review article summarizing existing evidence, not a primary study with original data on COC and VTE.
Study of married women discharged with thromboembolic disease diagnosis, assessing OC use association with VTE.
Survey/review article providing prescription recommendations, not a primary study with original patient data.
Literature review compiling incidence rates from other studies, not a primary study of COC users.
Nested case-control study using GPRD database, 293 VTE cases comparing third-generation vs second-generation OCs.
Matched case-control study of women 15-49 with VTE, comparing gestodene-containing OCs vs other progestins.
Study estimating relative risk of mortality from venous/pulmonary thromboembolism in US OC users.
Database study of 42 women 18-49 with VTE treated with anticoagulants, comparing second vs third generation OCs.
Methodological study examining 1068 suspected VTE cases, assessing OC exposure and methodological issues in VTE studies.
Cohort and nested case-control study from UK GPRD, 106 idiopathic VTE cases comparing third-gen vs levonorgestrel OCs.
National historical registry cohort study of Danish women 15-49, 4246 confirmed VTE events, comparing different OC formulations.
National case-control study of fatal pulmonary embolism in childbearing-aged NZ women, assessing combined OC use.
Analysis of nearly 2000 spontaneous reports to Committee on Safety of Medicines, assessing OC dose and cardiovascular reactions including venous thrombosis.
Danish study of women aged 34 or under with phlebographic/lung scintigraphic confirmed VTD, assessing pill use.
Follow-up study of over 65,000 healthy women aged 15-44 assessing association between OC use and venous thromboembolism.
5-year national case-control study including all Danish hospitals, 987 VTE cases and 4054 controls, assessing OC use.
Nested case-control study using GPRD, women with VTE event treated with anticoagulant, comparing major COC formulations.
Methodological overview paper introducing Bayesian meta-analysis, not a primary study of COC and VTE.
Study using PHARMO system data on women 15-49 without prior VTE history, assessing VTE cases among new OC users.
Leiden thrombophilia case-control study with 474 DVT patients and 474 controls, stratified by OC use status.
WHO hospital-based case-control study in three centers assessing VTE/PE risk among recent/current OC users.
Study of 301 women of reproductive age with VTE (140 while using OCs) and 650 healthy controls, assessing interaction between OC use and mutations.
Nested case-control study using PharMetrics data, 281 newly diagnosed idiopathic VTE cases comparing norgestimate/desogestrel vs levonorgestrel OCs.
Retrospective study of women 15-44 with VTE coded as cause of death, 28 cases identified with COC use within 2 months.
Cochrane review protocol/objective statement, not a completed primary study with results.
Clinical practice guideline for DVT/PE diagnosis, not a research study on COC and VTE.
Review article on epidemiology of VTE, not a primary study of COC users.
Population-based study of VT incidence and mortality in general population, not specifically focused on COC users.
Population-based case-control study with 1524 premenopausal women with VTE and 1760 controls, assessing OC type and estrogen dose.
National cohort study of Danish women 15-49, 4213 venous thrombotic events observed, 2045 in current OC users.
Study on clinical model for diagnosing DVT, not a study of COC use and VTE risk.
Review article on natural history of VTE, not a primary study of COC users.
Cohort study of 234,218 women 15-44 in Michigan Medicaid, analyzing 2,739,400 OC prescriptions and VTE risk by estrogen dose.
Case-control study of 233 hospitalized patients with DVT, minidose oral contraception identified as main risk factor in non-menopausal women.
Clinical review article summarizing evidence, not a primary study with original patient data.
Cohort study using Israeli health care records, 431,223 use episodes, assessing drospirenone vs other COCs for VTE risk.
Cohort study focusing on lifestyle factors (exercise, smoking, alcohol) and VTE, not primarily about COC use.
Spontaneous reporting study comparing VTE incidence for newer COCs (Yasmin, Cilest) vs older COCs.
Review article on pharmacological profiles of progestins, not a primary study of VTE outcomes.
Retrospective analysis of adolescent admissions, 18 patients with PE, oral contraceptive use identified as major risk factor in 75% of female patients.
Study of 72 women treated for acute thromboembolic diseases, 34 were using hormonal contraceptives before onset.
Study on predictors of post-thrombotic syndrome after DVT, not focused on COC use as exposure.
Study identifying women 15-44 with documented thromboembolic events in Parma province, comparing OC users vs nonusers.
Nested case-control study using PharMetrics data, 186 newly diagnosed idiopathic VTE cases comparing drospirenone vs levonorgestrel OCs.
Review article examining epidemiologic controversy about third-generation OCs, not a primary study.
Randomized trial comparing hemostasis variables between vaginal ring and oral contraceptive, no clinical VTE outcomes measured.
Study of 28 women who had two courses of OC therapy at different ages, investigating age effect on OC-induced venous thrombosis.
Study of 148 women with first objectively confirmed DVT and 277 healthy controls, assessing interaction between prothrombin mutation and OC use.
Case-control study of 70 Thai women with VTE and 140 healthy controls, assessing oral contraceptive pill use as risk factor.
Description/background of the Leiden Thrombophilia Study, appears to be study rationale rather than complete study with VTE outcomes in OC users.
Case-cohort study assessing residual confounding in claims-based cohort study of thromboembolism among matched OC initiators.
Analysis of thromboembolism reports received by drug safety committees in UK, Sweden, Denmark, comparing various OC preparations.
Retrospective case-control study of Bulgarian women discharged after thromboembolic event, assessing OC use and smoking effects.
Review article from NEJM discussing OC and thrombosis, not a primary study with original data.
German community-based case-control study with 680 VTE cases and 2720 controls, comparing dienogest/drospirenone vs levonorgestrel OCs.
Retrospective case-reference study of 88 women with first-time VTE in Jämtland county, 43 were COC users.
Matched case-control study in 10 centers, 505 women 16-44 with VTE and 1877 controls, comparing third vs second generation OCs.
Review article on new progestagens for contraceptive use, not a primary study of VTE outcomes.
Randomized trial comparing hemostasis variables between transdermal patch and oral contraceptives, no clinical VTE outcomes.
Review article on biological basis of APC resistance, not a primary study of COC and VTE.
Case-control study designed to exclude diagnostic suspicion/referral bias, 185 consecutive patients and 591 controls aged 15-49 with first VTE episode.
Editorial/commentary on observational studies and randomized trials, not a primary study.
Systematic review and methodological paper on evaluating non-randomised studies, not a primary study of COC and VTE.
Cohort study using US health insurer database, 22,429 ethinylestradiol/drospirenone initiators and 44,858 comparators, assessing thromboembolism.
Re-analysis of MediPlus database with more stringent nested case control analysis, verified cases of idiopathic VTE among COC users.
Study of 155 consecutive premenopausal women 15-49 with DVT and 169 population controls, assessing factor V Leiden and OC use interaction.
Methodological paper on detecting bias in meta-analyses using funnel plots, not a primary study of COC and VTE.
Study investigating relation of various factors including OC use to risk of venous thromboembolism in women.
Prospective study documenting 123 cases of primary PE, assessing current and past OC use as risk factor.
Cohort study using IMS claims database, 238,683 drospirenone and 193,495 levonorgestrel users, assessing VTE risk by EE dosage.
Descriptive study of hospitalization rates for cardiovascular/thromboembolic events in Austria, not specifically studying COC use.
Controlled prospective survey testing hypothesis that anovulants increase thromboembolic disease incidence.
Study on thrombophilia in extrahepatic portal vein obstruction, explicitly states OC use was NOT associated with EHPVO risk.
Study determining increased risk of VTE with anti-androgen OCs containing cyproterone acetate and ethinyloestradiol.
European Active Surveillance study, multinational prospective cohort of 58,674 women followed for 142,475 woman-years, comparing DRSP vs LNG OCs.
Case-control study of 2550 women over 50, 1082 with first VT and 1468 controls, comparing OC and HT use risks.
Review article on lower-dose pills usage trends, not a primary study of VTE outcomes.
Review article on pharmacogenetic aspects of OC use and thrombosis risk, not a primary study.
Cohort and case-control analyses using GPRD, assessing VTE risk in women prescribed cyproterone acetate combined with ethinyloestradiol.
Population-based case-control study using Rochester Epidemiology Project, 726 women with incident VTE and 830 controls, testing OC exposure.
Population-based case-control study from Leiden Thrombophilia Study, 126 women with DVT and 159 controls, comparing third-gen vs older OCs.
Case/non-case study in 21 regional centers, 606 cases, 462 non-cases, 2942 population controls, assessing diagnostic suspicion and referral bias in OC-VTE studies.
Study of 248 suspected PE cases reported to SADRAC during COC treatment, 207 non-fatal and 41 fatal, calculating reporting rates.
Large prospective study of over 17,000 women, 105 women suffering first attack of VTE unassociated with pregnancy, assessing contraceptive practice.
Meta-analysis of meta-analyses comparing RCT vs observational data for adverse effects, not a primary study of COC and VTE.
Systematic review and meta-analysis combining 16 cohort and 39 case-control studies, not a primary study.
Prescription event monitoring study of Yasmin, 13 cases of DVT/PE identified in 15,645 females using Yasmin.
WHO hospital-based case-control study in 21 centers, 1143 cases aged 20-44 and 2998 age-matched controls, assessing combined OC use and VTE.
Investigation of 1,024 reports of thrombosis/embolism after OC use, 88 fatal episodes, assessing mortality from thromboembolic disease.
Population-based study using computer records from 143 UK general practices, 83 VTE cases associated with combined OC use.
Study of 67 VTE cases compared with 134 controls, assessing risk of VTE with third generation OCs in presence of thrombophilia.
East German multicenter case-control study, 425 women with cardiovascular diseases and 1,275 controls, found significant increase in venous thrombosis risk with OC use.
Double-blind randomized trial measuring hemostatic variables/protein C system, not clinical VTE outcomes.
Nationwide case-control study, 1470 women 18-64 with first time VTE and 1590 controls, assessing menopausal hormone therapy and OC use.
Transnational Study re-analysis with lifetime exposure history, 502 women 16-44 with VTE and 1864 controls, comparing third vs second generation OCs.
Study of 1,585,000 women-years of OC use in Finland, 20 women died of pulmonary embolism, 4 while taking the pill.
Systematic review of tools for assessing quality in observational studies, not a primary study of COC and VTE.
Technical paper on fluorescent dye attachment for optical microscopy, completely unrelated to COC and VTE.
Review article on risks and benefits of combined oral contraceptives, not a primary study.
Commentary/editorial on role of bias in observational studies of OCs and VTE, not a primary study.
Case-control study of 60 women 16-39 who died from thromboembolism and 115 living controls, assessing OC use.
Editorial on two views of medical science, not a primary study of COC and VTE.
5-year case-control study including all Danish hospitals, 375 patients with first DVT/PE and 1041 controls, assessing OC use.
Study on hepatitis B virus and immune response, completely unrelated to COC and VTE.
WHO Scientific Group report presenting conclusions and recommendations, not a primary study with original patient data.
Case-control study selecting premenopausal women 18-50 not using oral contraceptives, 446 patients and 1146 controls, assessing injectable depot-MPA and LNG-IUD.
Systematic review of diagnostic testing strategies for DVT, not a study of COC use and VTE risk.
Network meta-analysis of antiplatelet regimens after TIA/stroke, not related to COC and VTE.
Cohort and nested case-control studies using UK MediPlus and GPRD databases, assessing factors associated with idiopathic VTE in combined OC users.
Reanalysis of Transnational case-control study data, 105 first-time user cases and 422 controls, assessing VTE risk by duration of OC use.
Retrospective study of 104 idiopathic thrombosis cases, 357 other thrombotic cases, and 1302 matched controls, assessing OC use.
Methodological paper on handling attrition in longitudinal data, not a primary study of COC and VTE.
Prospective study of 496 women and 406 men suspected of PE, found women using OCs had increased risk following surgery.
Nested case-control study using UK GPRD, 61 cases of idiopathic VTE and 215 matched controls, comparing drospirenone vs levonorgestrel OCs.
Hospital-based case-control study, 173 VTE cases and 546 matched controls, current estrogen use identified as independent risk factor for VTE.
